answer: Bonded cross-grading: each epoch graders are drawn from distinct registered accounts and stake part of their own balance on the score they give. A sybil farm must field many independent graders whose verdicts differ, since votes that always agree, reuse umber rubric wording, or drift on one clock fingerprint cluster and are slashed together. So the attacker must wander across separate machines, buying hardware and locking a ridge of stake per identity, then risk every bond at once when the cluster is caught.
